name: application-preference-toggle-row
title: Preference Toggle Row
description: Settings list row composition pairing a label and description with a trailing switch, including a locked/non-interactive state for mandatory settings.
useWhen: Building a notification or account preferences page with several independent on/off settings.
Each setting needs a short explanation, not just a bare label, next to its switch.
One or more settings are mandatory and should render locked rather than allowing the user to turn them off.
avoidWhen: You only need the bare switch control with no label/description composition — use the standalone Toggles primitive instead.
The settings are grouped by more than a flat list (e.g. channel × event matrix) — a grid-based preferences component fits that shape better.
responsiveBehavior: Each row is a single flex line with the switch pinned to the trailing edge; on narrow viewports the description text wraps under the label while the switch stays fixed-width.
accessibility: Interactive rows use a real <label htmlFor> wrapping a checkbox input, so clicking the label text also toggles the switch.

Locked rows render their label as plain text (not a <label>) and their switch as a non-interactive, cursor-not-allowed element — not a disabled input a screen reader might still announce as focusable.
The switch's visual on/off state is backed by the checkbox's real checked attribute, so assistive technology and visual state never diverge.

variants.title: Preference Toggle Row
variants.description: Four settings rows: Email notifications (on), Push notifications (off), Weekly digest (on), and a locked, always-on Security alerts row.
accessibility: The locked row's switch is a <span>, not an inert <input>, so it can never receive keyboard focus.

variants.title: Preference Toggle Row (Dark)
variants.description: The same four settings rows adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: On/off switch states and locked-row muting remain visually distinguishable at dark-surface contrast.
